 Republican Anthony Constantino declared victory in the tight race for New York’s 21st Congressional District, then used his election-night speech to criticize his Democratic opponent and the media.
 Constantino, the CEO of Sticker Mule, thanked the Trump family, Vice President JD Vance, Rudy Giuliani and Roger Stone. He also thanked his mother, supporters, campaign staff, friends and Sticker Mule employees.
 He criticized Blake Gendebien, telling voters, "You had a chance to vote for somebody that loves us," said Constantino. "Blake Gendebien hates us."
 Constantino also blamed media coverage for forcing him to spend heavily on the race.
 "They spent the whole time lying to the citizens of NY-21 about Blake Gendebien," said Constantino.
 He accused reporters of not telling voters about his job creation and taxes. Later, he called them a bunch of "f---ing a---holes," and directed more profanity at others in the crowd. Constantino also repeatedly attacked a reporter and eventually kicked him out during the speech.
 Constantino said he spent $17 million of his own money on the campaign and was disappointed the race was close. Results were still coming in when he said, "Three or four points," Constantino said as results were still coming in, "which is disappointing for me because I want to win by 20."
 He also called for President Donald Trump to pardon Sean “Diddy” Combs, who is serving time after being convicted on prostitution-related charges.
 Constantino announced a $1,000 bonus for Sticker Mule employees and urged other companies to do the same.
 "I'm officially asking every company in the United States of America, particularly the large ones, if you can swing it and you got cash in the bank, cut a check to your workers and give them a thousand dollar bonus."
 The speech drew national attention, including coverage from TMZ and a segment on The Daily Show that focused on Constantino’s profanity and the removal of a Watertown reporter. A young child was seen in the front row during the speech. 
 Constantino, when asked about his comments about Diddy by a TMZ reporter, stated that he wanted to make New York exciting again, and that Diddy made New York exciting.
